This page presents the eight-stage **Theory / Understand path**, followed by a progressive resource map. The **Build path is independent**: it has its own implementation order and entry point. The route is derived from the canonical curriculum; the map starts from the high-level territories, then reveals sections and pages as you click. The reading notes below collapse by default; the map mirrors the search, filter, and selection in the URL, and the "Copy link" button shares that exact view.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How to read this map"}

- **Territories** — the main parts of the site: Understand, Build, Practice, Deepen, Reference.
- **Sections** — clicking a territory reveals its subsections; the breadcrumb or the Escape key takes you back up one level.
- **Pages** — clicking a page shows its details (purpose, sections, links); "Open the page" navigates there directly.
- **Concepts** — the "Canonical concepts" view groups the concepts from the bilingual registry versioned in `data/concepts.yml` by discovery domain, with their definitions, typed relationships, and resource pages. The search and the relation-type filter narrow the list, a selected concept highlights its neighbours, and related concepts remain clickable from the details panel.

Section headings shown in a page's details are editorial landmarks, not canonical concepts. The map must not be interpreted as a single reading order: the guided route below plays that role.

:::

::: {.guided-route-section}

## Theory path — Understand

This theory path first answers three questions: what is an LLM, how does it compute a prediction, and what can be done with that prediction? The first part places the system in context; the second covers four stages, from text to the next-token distribution; the third presents three sibling uses, generating, scoring an observed target, and learning by updating the parameters, which are not successive prerequisites. Evaluation remains cross-cutting: it measures the model on held-out data ([experimental evaluation](experimental-evaluation.qmd)). The eight detailed stages remain the suggested progression: core pages cover each stage's main ideas; optional resources offer further context or depth and can belong to any destination. Pages within a stage are complementary resources, not a list of strict prerequisites.

{{< include ../includes/generated-guided-route-en.qmd >}}

::: {.guided-route-companion}

**Other primary path — Build:** To build a small GPT, follow the [independent Build path](build-path.html). It has its own implementation milestones and prerequisites; it is not a required continuation of the Theory path. Corpus preparation and training-example construction form a dedicated model-learning branch, not a prerequisite for inference.

:::

:::

## Explore the resources

These views support exploration; they do not replace the guided route above (territories, sections, pages, and concepts are described at the top of the page). The "Reset view" button clears the search, the filter, and the selection; "Copy link" copies the URL of the current view; the Escape key steps back one level at a time. Both the map and the list below are generated automatically by the Python meta-code from the Quarto sidebar and page metadata: a single source to maintain.
